file-catalog-with-saved-data-01.graded_text: Saved data is reached through the same read, write, exact-edit, and delete-file tools used for source files and assets, as file paths such as JSON files. The catalog has no separate tools for records, entries, collections, or the database.

votes.e: A/project/docs/mcp-tools.md catalog table lines 162-169 add separate saved-data tools: "| `list_entries` | Lists or searches saved-data entries in a collection |", "| `create_entries` |", "| `update_entries` | Patches saved-data entries |", "| `delete_entries` |", "| `delete_all_entries` | Empties one collection |", plus `get_data_rules`/`set_data_rules`. Line 366: "Agents get the same entry-by-entry view of saved data that visitors get... with nothing like an \"edit the whole dataset\" operation." Saved data is never reached through read_file/replace_files/edit_file/delete_files as JSON file paths.

file-catalog-with-saved-data-02.graded_text: No tool has a required idempotency key, revision or version token, or confirmation argument. Protection against stale writes is enforced by the server, for example by rejecting a write that would overwrite changes made since the agent's read and asking for a fresh read.

votes.e: A/project/docs/mcp-tools.md line 308 (replace_files): "expected_revision: string;   // required; get it from list_files or a previous write"; line 385 (set_data_rules): "expected_revision: string;"; line 458 (update_entries): "expected_revision: string | null;   // required"; line 470: "**`expected_revision` is a required field.**" These are required caller-supplied revision tokens, not server-enforced staleness checks.

file-catalog-with-saved-data-03.graded_text: The design explains how a visitor's write made after the agent read a saved-data file survives the agent's later write of that file: it is merged safely or the agent's write fails with a conflict. A plain last-writer-wins replacement does not pass.

votes.e: A/project/docs/mcp-tools.md line 472: "Pass `null` for a change that stands on its own... The merge patch touches only the listed fields, so a visitor ticking a different field of the same entry is kept." With expected_revision null, a visitor's write to the same field made after the agent's read is silently overwritten (field-level last-writer-wins); the conflict path (line 471) is only taken if the agent opts in. There is also no saved-data file whose whole-file write is reconciled.

file-catalog-with-saved-data-04.graded_text: Deleting files takes an explicit nonempty list of exact paths, deleting a whole site is its own tool, and no omitted argument widens a deletion or makes an update create a new site.

votes.e: A/project/docs/mcp-tools.md line 350 (delete_files): "paths: string[];     // 1–100 items"; line 355: "not_found, index_required" so no path widens; line 239 delete_site is its own tool "input:  { site_id: string }"; line 320 (replace_files): "Refuses paths that don't exist... It never creates a file by accident."; create_site (line 222) is the only site-creating tool and no update tool takes an optional workspace/site that would create one. Closest risk: line 500 delete_all_entries "input:  { site_id: string; collection: string }", but it is a separate tool with no omitted-argument widening (line 506).

file-catalog-with-saved-data-05.graded_text: Writing a saved-data file as a whole is checked entry by entry against the site's declared write rules and validation, with the agent holding only the rights of the person it acts for, so replacing the whole file cannot make a change that person could not make one entry at a time.

votes.e: A/project/docs/mcp-tools.md line 128: "// Applies to visitors. Workspace members, and agents acting for them, may always do everything."; line 366: "an agent acts for a workspace member, so data rules never limit it."; line 582: "There's no per-field rules or value-schema validation yet." Agent writes are not checked against the site's declared rules or validation at all, and there is no whole-file write checked entry by entry.

file-catalog-with-saved-data-06.graded_text: There is no separate tool or argument for setting a site's title, description, or favicon. They come from index.html.

votes.e: A/project/docs/mcp-tools.md line 215 (get_site): "Title, description, and favicon come from `index.html` every time the site is read. To change them, edit `index.html`. No tool sets them directly."; Assumption 4 line 576. Checked create_site input (line 222-225: only workspace_id and files) and all 19 tools in the table at lines 149-169; none takes title/description/favicon.
